data.name: Nerielle
data.gender_notes: Nerielle is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nerielle is derived from the Hebrew name Neriah, which means 'light of God'. In the Bible, Neriah was a scribe and a prince, a man of the Chaldeans who held a high position in King Jehoiakim's court. He is mentioned in Jeremiah 32:12, where he is described as a 'faithful man who stands before the Lord'. The name Nerielle carries the meaning “Light of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nerielle usually hope their child will grow to embody light of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Nerielle belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nerielle total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_greek.name: Νεριέλλη
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Νεριέλλη είναι μια ονομασία που περιλαμβάνει την ιδέα της αθανασίας, της ανθούσας ψυχής, της ζωής και της μορφής. Με την ανάμνηση του Νεραίων, το όνομα συνδέεται με την αθανασία και την ισότητα. Οι εκκλησιαστικές παραδόσεις συνδέουν την ονομασία με την ιδέα της αθανάτου ψυχής.

in_latin.name: Neriella
in_latin.long_meaning: Neriella est nomen quod includit notionem immortalitatis, animi floris, vitae et formae. Cum memoria Neeraionis, nomen connectitur ad immortalitatem et aequalitatem. Ecclesiasticae traditiones Neriellam nominem connectunt ad notionem animae immortalis.

biblical_reference.note: Nerielle is not a direct biblical name, but rather an interpretation of Nerian or Neri

historical_references.reference: The character Nerielle appears in the 13th century French apocryphal text 'The Golden Legend' as a virgin martyr. She is said to have been a noblewoman from Tarsus in Cilicia who converted to Christianity and was persecuted for her faith under the Roman emperor Diocletian. Her resistance to Roman persecution led to her martyrdom.

Another reference to Nerielle can be found in the 16th century Italian hagiography 'Acta Sanctorum' where she is mentioned as a martyr of the Roman persecutions under Diocletian. The text describes her as a noblewoman from Syria who, along with her husband and three sons, was martyred for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nerielle is of French origin, and it is derived from the Hebrew name Nelia, meaning 'miracle' or 'wonder'. In modern contexts, this name is often used in fantasy literature, where characters with the name Nerielle are typically magical, ethereal beings. On platforms such as Goodreads, readers can discover and discuss books featuring characters named Nerielle. In role-playing games, such as those played on Tabletop Simulator, the name Nerielle is often given to elven or other magical characters. Additionally, the name Nerielle has gained popularity in the fashion industry, with some individuals using it as a unique and evocative name for personal brands or social media accounts. On Instagram, for example, users with the name Nerielle may post content related to fashion, beauty, or the supernatural, further emphasizing the mystical and ethereal connotations of the name.
